content: The National Tobacco Cessation Collaborative (NTCC) operates in the United States and Canada through the combined efforts of dedicated organizations. These collaborative members include major organizations that fund research, programs, and policy initiatives related to tobacco cessation, as well as other entities with a vested interest in promoting tobacco cessation. The NTCC adheres to seven guiding principles in all its activities: 1. All activities must be grounded in the best available scientific evidence. 2. Coordinated efforts are essential to achieve the greatest impact. 3. Collaboration among multiple stakeholders, including public and private entities, is necessary to make progress. 4. Increasing tobacco cessation requires the removal of barriers and the facilitation of systemic changes. 5. The most effective dissemination techniques should be employed to implement key strategies successfully. 6. Implementation efforts must be rigorously evaluated. 7. Research should be supported to identify more effective tobacco cessation interventions and methods for disseminating these interventions. The collaborative includes a wide range of member organizations, such as: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality American Academy of Family Physicians American Cancer Society American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists American Heart Association American Legacy Foundation American Lung Association American Nurses Association American Public Health Association American Society of Clinical Oncology Arizona Cancer Center Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids Canadian Tobacco Control Research Initiative C-Change Cecil G. Sheps Center for Health Services Research, University of North Carolina Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Center for Tobacco Research and Intervention, University of Wisconsin College of Medicine, University of Vermont Environmental Protection Agency Health Resources and Services Administration Institute for Health Research and Policy, University of Illinois at Chicago Johns Hopkins School of Public Health National Cancer Institute National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute National Institute on Drug Abuse National Partnership to Help Pregnant Smokers Quit North American Quitline Consortium Partnership for Prevention Robert Wood Johnson Foundation Substance Abuse & Mental Health Services Administration Tobacco-Free Coalition of Oregon United States Department of Veterans Affairs Vancouver Hospital and Health Sciences Centre Membership in the NTCC is open to any organization committed to increasing successful tobacco cessation and improving public health. However, member organizations must not engage in activities that conflict with the goal of improving public health. All members are required to adhere to the guiding principles of the NTCC.
